title: Every Atlas Document version is retained permanently, so the tree is an append-only record
content:
A.1.2.1.2.2 specifies that when an Atlas Document is modified its version number increments "and the old version is recorded as a historical version with a Document Identifier equivalent to its version number" — a document at 1.1.1 version 3 becomes 1.1.1.v4, with the prior text preserved at 1.1.1.v3. The stated purpose: "This ensures all historical versions of Atlas documents are retained permanently as a part of the Atlas."

The non-obvious part is *where* the history lives. Superseded versions are not archived elsewhere or kept in a changelog; they receive real Document Identifiers inside the tree. History is therefore addressable and citable by the same mechanism as current text, which means an argument about precedent or about what a rule used to require can point at a document rather than at a diff.

This is what makes precedent-bound interpretation (A.1.1.2) actually workable. Congruence with established precedent requires knowing what the text said when a precedent was set; permanent, addressable versions supply that. It also makes silent revision impossible — you cannot change what a rule appeared to say, only add a version.

A.1.2.1.2.1 completes the picture from the other side: the human-readable Name property "can be modified with no substantive consequences" because the official designation is the Document Identifier. Labels are cheap and mutable; addresses and history are not.
description: A.1.2.1.2.2 files each superseded version at an identifier suffixed with its version number (1.1.1.v3), making revision history part of the Atlas itself rather than external metadata.
